notes: Twenty original fictional U.S. market-microstructure teaching cases; source references are educational starting points, not blanket proof of source rights or broker executions; no grade or lookahead.

guides.title: A displayed bid quantity is an offer to buy, not a guaranteed sale fill
guides.concept: A bid identifies a stated willing purchase price and displayed quantity under a particular feed; order priority, cancellations and other venues determine what remains executable.
guides.procedure: Take a time-stamped bid snapshot, define round-lot and odd-lot units, then compare displayed quantity with subsequent independently recorded executions.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A $10.00 bid shows 300 shares at 09:30:00. A learner wishes to sell 400 shares. The 300 displayed shares cannot establish whether even 300 will still be available when an order reaches the venue.
guides.limit: A quote may cancel or be bypassed; size at one venue is not consolidated guaranteed liquidity.
guides.invalidation: The teaching interpretation stops if required event time, feed status or eligible input is missing: A quote may cancel or be bypassed; size at one venue is not consolidated guaranteed liquidity.

guides.title: An ask quantity is a time-specific selling interest, not stock already purchased
guides.concept: An ask represents offered shares at a named price; it says nothing by itself about a later buyer's fill or aggregate market supply.
guides.procedure: Identify best offer, displayed size, time and quote venue before inferring what a marketable buy might encounter.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: The ask is $10.05 for 100 shares, but a fictional learner considers 250. The display does not entitle that order to 100 at $10.05; another participant can execute or cancel first.
guides.limit: Multiple venues, hidden liquidity and quote updates prevent interpreting one screen as a deterministic execution schedule.

guides.concept: Market centers update independently; the information-feed timestamp and protected quote rules must be reconciled before comparisons.
guides.procedure: Record each venue's price, time, security class and feed; distinguish local best bid/offer from applicable consolidated protected NBBO.

guides.title: A print at a displayed bid does not prove the seller's motive
guides.concept: Comparing execution price to contemporaneous bid/offer is a classification heuristic; hidden interest, crossed quotes and asynchrony produce ambiguity.
guides.procedure: Align exchange-eligible trade and quote timestamps; label inferred aggressor side as uncertain rather than an observed customer intention.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Trade $10.00 prints while aligned bid/ask are $10.00/$10.03. It may be classified bid-side by a heuristic, but the print alone cannot show whether the participant is exiting, hedging or opening risk.

guides.title: The quote midpoint is arithmetic, not necessarily an available order price
guides.concept: A quoted midpoint is halfway between eligible best bid and offer; it is a reference price used in analysis, not an assured execution.
guides.procedure: Check quote eligibility, calculate (bid+offer)/2, then separately inspect the actual execution evidence.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Bid $10.00 and offer $10.06 give midpoint $10.03. A $10.03 midpoint label does not prove any resting share can actually be bought or sold there.

guides.title: Locked and crossed quote states require explicit validity handling
guides.concept: A locked best market has equal bid and offer; a crossed market has bid above offer, and published reporting rules may treat those states differently.
guides.procedure: Validate bid/ask and quote times, flag equality and inversion, and do not force a negative quoted spread to look normal.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Bid $15.01 and offer $15.00 are crossed, producing −$0.01 arithmetic spread. Reporting and order-quality analysis must recognize the abnormal state instead of treating the negative number as cheap liquidity.
guides.limit: Specific 2026 Rule 605 reporting exemptions and benchmark treatment apply in defined contexts, not to every trading calculation.

guides.title: The number of tape prints is not traded share volume
guides.concept: One reported execution message can describe one or many shares; trade count and aggregate eligible share count have different units.
guides.procedure: Sum each eligible final execution quantity to compute shares and separately count eligible executions after correction handling.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: Three eligible trades of 100, 400 and 25 shares produce trade count=3 but reported volume=525 shares. A histogram labeled 525 trades would be false.
guides.limit: Some feeds aggregate or split trades and include condition codes; count of messages is not always count of independent executions.
